utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar, could you call the case please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case Number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, registrar. And good morning to you. Mr. Oric, can you hear me in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. I can understand everything that's being said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning to you. Please take your seat. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. My name is Jan Wubben, senior trial attorney, together with counsel, Mr. Gramsci Di Fazio and Ms. Joanne Richardson, and our case manager, Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben, and good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Vasvija Vidovic appearing together with Mr. John Jones for Naser Oric. We are joined today here by our legal assistant, Ms. Jasmina Cosic, and our CaseMap manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Ms. Vidovic, and good morning to you and your team. Just to put you into the picture, I will be signing this morning -- actually, I'm signing them now, our decision on Prosecution motion for the testimony of a witness of -- basically of witness -- the witnesses Radenko Zivanovic and Svetlana Trifunovic for the testimony of these two witnesses via video conference link. And it's taken that the days that you are seeking for these videolinks remain the 25 and the 26th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I will be signing this motion, granting the motion. There is also another decision that we will be handing down this morning and that is a decision on Prosecution's motion for the admission of written statements of witnesses Bogicevic, Bozic, and Bogdanovic. And we are referring only to the written statement of deceased witness Bozicevic, and we will be granting the motion. And then there is pending a motion, confidential motion, for protective measures relating to a particular witness who you seek to refer to as C008. We have a draft ready, but we will keep the draft pending until we interview this witness. In other words, the instructions for the time being are: Bring this witness along when you require him to give evidence. Do not in any way even remotely hint that he stands a good chance of getting any of these protective measures that you seek for him. We want to make sure that you do not make him live that illusion in case it does not materialise. And then on the basis of what he testifies here in private session, we will decide whether to go ahead and grant him the protective measures that you are seeking or not. It will be a very simple exercise. The decision will be given orally there and then. We have it written already either way; in other words, because we don't know exactly -- I mean, we are still very much undecided, very much undecided. So much depends on his reaction in the courtroom and the soundness of his concerns for his own safety. So, Madam registrar -- not Madam Registrar --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So can you bring in the witness --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have any preliminaries before we proceed with the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How long -- how much longer do you need, Ms. Richardson?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at most I anticipate an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: At most. Possibly an hour, if not less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you, Mr. Jones, you had to revise your according to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. I would certainly think two hours at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So let's bring the witness in. That's two hours plus an hour and a half, three hours and a half. That's more or less it. The sooner we finish, the better. Now what's happening to them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Stevanovic. Welcome back. Madam Usher is going to give you again -- hand to you the text of the solemn declaration. I would like you to read it out again today. I just want to remind you that you are still testifying under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, sir. You may sit down and we will be proceeding straight away with the direct -- with the examination-in-chief. Yes, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, when we left off yesterday - good morning to you - you were describing to us what you heard as you were escaping the attack on your village in June of 1992. I would like to take you back there again today. And I believe that you testified to yesterday was that you heard crying of someone that you knew. And if you could just tell us after you heard the crying what you proceeded to do after this -- after you heard the crying.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was nothing that I could do. I was in the creek and I couldn't get there. It was Ljubisa Gajic, the person I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did you later learn what happened to Ljubisa Gajic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Could you tell us.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just behind me as we were getting out of the creek, Milutin Stevanovic stayed behind. He never went down into the creek with me to begin with. And he watched the whole situation unfold. He told me that Ljubisa was wounded on the road, that he cried for help and moaned. He said the Muslims came over and took him over into the cornfield and burned him alive right there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Was the body of Mr. Ljubisa Gajic ever discovered?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His bones were found right there in the ashes. It all burned down together with the cornstalks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And if you could tell us if you know when did his bones -- when were his bones discovered?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not certain because I wasn't present myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Fine. Very well. Did Milutin Stevanovic -- this is a relative of yours?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a distant relative.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did he tell you about encountering -- did he tell you who had killed Mr. Gajic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A man named Ramco from Mocevici, but I don't know his last name.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And when you said that the Muslims came and took him, which Muslims are you referring to? Are you talking about civilians or soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did Mr. Stevanovic -- now, if you could tell us -- excuse me. If you could tell us what happened after you left the creek as you were fleeing, were you able to see any other villages burning?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from right there. I could no longer see my village or any other village for that matter from the creek.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And what direction did you flee in?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards the river, the river that led towards the Drina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: If I could ask for the usher's assistance at this time. I would request that this witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 407, which is the map that we used yesterday, with Your Honours' permission.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: If you could take a look at Prosecution Exhibit 407. Could you show us, point on that map the direction you took when you fled your village.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I ran down along this creek and went down as far as the river Grabovacka Rijeka, that's its name, which leads all the way to the river Drina itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could we zoom in the spot that the witness is indicating, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I went down as far as this river. I crossed the river below the village of Kaludra. I took cover in the woods there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. For the record, the witness indicates a route that starts somewhere in the vicinity of Bradjevina on the left-hand side of the circle, of the coloured circle on the map. In a south-easterly direction in the direction of Kaludra -- of Kaludra. Just where the tip of the arrow which he had indicated during yesterday's testimony is. Yeah. Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I crossed this river, and I reached the meadow behind the village of Kaludra in the direction of Grabovacka Rijeka to the right. The direction that I was headed from, I turned around and I saw my village ablaze, all of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And where did you go -- when you said you were hiding in the bushes, you said you went towards the Drina river. Could you show us the path you took to get to the Drina River.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I came out of the creek. I crossed the river below the village of Kaludra, and I crossed these meadows to the right of the river and through the woods. There were woods there and meadows, and I went down as far as Grabovacka Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And could you point to Grabovacka Rijeka on the map if you see it.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, the witness points to Grabovacka Rijeka on the map. Could you put it in a circle or draw an "X" in a circle there and put your signature -- your initials nearby, please. Just put an "X" in a circle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but you didn't put an "X."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And put your initials outside the circle, please, top right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, could you tell us who you were fleeing with, who was in your presence as you were going towards the Grabovacka Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My father, Radivoje; my mother, Zorka; my brother, Slavko; a relative named Djuro; a relative named Milovan; a man named Milutin who stayed behind in the creek; a man named Mile Petrovic from the neighbouring village of Magudovici; a man named Milojko Stjepanovic also from the neighbouring village of Magudovici. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: You said a couple of these individuals were from the neighbouring village of Magudovici. Could you tell us if --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mile Milojko.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Could you tell us if you are aware of any other villages that were attacked that day in your neighbouring village, and that includes Magudovici.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Magudovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: In addition to Magudovici, were there any other villages attacked that day in the immediate vicinity of Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kaludra and Vranesevici.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, if I could ask for the usher's assistance again, and I would refer you to the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And ask if those villages you just mentioned are on the map. I believe they were circled previously, but if you could just for the record indicate with an "X" next to those villages that were also attacked on the same day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Does he have to indicate with an "X" this time?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I only want to make the record clear because later on as we are looking at this map there are some circles indicating previously that these were Serb villages. What I'd like for him to do now is indicate which Serb villages that he previously circled were also attacked. I think it's important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On the map there is only one village indicated which was not a Serb village. All the ones in red are Serb villages. The one in yellow or the blue is the only Muslim one. So if he says --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, they weren't all --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If he says "Kaludra," we can see it and that's it. So let's proceed. I don't want him to mark anything. Let's move.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: As you wish, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, with respect to these villages, could you tell us if you were able to see as you were fleeing towards the river, if you were able to see these villages and see if there was any burning taking place.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Behind me was the village of Kaludra. I could only smell smoke. I couldn't see the village itself. As for the village of Vranesevici it had not been torched at that point in time yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did you later learn that it had been?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And what did you learn? What were you told?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came back from Grabovacka Rijeka, my relatives Milutin and Stevan didn't come. Stojan Stevanovic was also not there, but he had not come with us to Grabovacka Rijeka to begin with. There was a group ahead of me that went straight to the village of Bradjevina. I don't know who those people were but I did know some of them. I followed them after a while, although the Serbs at Grabovacka Rijeka were trying to keep me from going. They said that I would get myself killed as well. I had to go there because my brother remained in the village. I headed towards that village. I approached the village of Vranesevici. I met a man named Stanisa Stevanovic; also Borivoje Milanovic, Sreten Stjepanovic, who hails from Vranesevici. I mean Sreten. They were driving Stojan on a cart. I saw that Stojan's throat had been cut, and I saw that the far end of the village of Vranesevici was beginning to catch fire. I saw things strewn along the roadsides, some sort of bags or backpacks containing food mostly. And I went straight back to Grabovacka Rijeka from there with them. I never returned to my village or to any other village in the area after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: The men who were fleeing with you, did they -- from Magudovici, did they mention what had happened to their village? Did they say why they were fleeing?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said to me that in Magudovici everything had been burned down, destroyed, that they barely managed to get out of the village. And it just so happened that they came to the creek where I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would request that we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are back in open session now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, as you returned -- you said at some point you encountered Stanisa Stevanovic with the body of Stojan. I should ask, is Stojan a relative of yours?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And what did -- in addition to seeing the body with Stanisa, what did Stanisa say to you with respect to the village of Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said to me that he saw some of the people who did that, that these were Muslim extremists, or rather soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did he say anything about the state of the village?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village was completely destroyed, burned down.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did there --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And he said to me that my house, the house that I was born in, our old house, and the barn that was nearby in the middle of the village. And there were about two tonnes of wheat in that barn, he told me that that had remained intact and that it had not burned down at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because I need to clear this. It may have been my hearing, which is usually very good. But your question was this: "And what did -- in addition to seeing the body with Stanisa, what did Stanisa say to you with respect to the village of Bradjevina?" And the answer was: "He said to me that he saw some of the people who did it, that they were Muslim extremists, or rather soldiers." Did you say that they were Muslim extremists or rather soldiers, or did you say that they were Muslim extremists rather than soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which one is the correct one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's all the same. It's one in the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Let me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One means that you are assimilating Muslim extremists with soldiers; to you they are one and the same thing. The other one is you are distinguishing Muslim extremists from soldiers. One says these were Muslim extremists or rather soldiers. The other one says these were Muslim extremists rather than soldiers. It's important that he gets the interpretation correct here because the first translation that I heard myself said rather than soldiers and not -- or rather soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, could you tell us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let him answer the question, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was trying to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. Let him -- I think the question has been clear enough.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Soldier -- soldiers and extremists had the same uniforms, the same objectives. For me it was one and the same thing. They had the same objective, to destroy everything that was Serb, and that's what they did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Exactly. That's your answer. You may proceed, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did you ever return to the village of Bradjevina and could you tell us what year this was?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned after the Dayton Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Can you recall the year and the approximate month?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was towards the end of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And could you --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Could you tell us what you saw in the village when you returned.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I returned to the village, I couldn't recognise anything. There were weeds and grass all over and I barely managed to find my own house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And what were the -- was the state of your house?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the stone foundations were there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And did you see the other houses in the village?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. They looked the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Since the attack in 1992 in June did you return to the village to live -- well, I guess I should ask: Since the attack in 1992, did anyone ever return to Bradjevina, yourself or the other villagers, to reside there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And could you tell us why you didn't return or any of the other villagers.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had nowhere to go. And until 1994 and 1995, all these Serb villages were under Muslim control.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And the state of the houses themselves, were they destroyed so that no one could return there to live immediately after the attack? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. No one had any place to return to. There was just ashes, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did you or any of your fellow villagers from Bradjevina receive compensation for the damage to your home from the Muslim forces or the Muslim military?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did you or anyone in the village that you know of receive compensation for the loss of the animals, the livestock, that was taken from the village during the attack?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not until now, no one gave us anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: So you've never received anything?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did you ever learn who was responsible for the attack on your village and the surrounding villages that day?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the Srebrenica Muslim army, Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, you -- let me just -- I'd like to cover a particular area with you. You mentioned that one of your brothers had fled with you. Could you tell us what happened to your other brother.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My other brother was in the village. From the position where I was, I couldn't see anything. He was also wounded. At a point that was lower than the village in the wheat fields. He was trying to get out. He was hiding in the wheat fields, and that's where he got two wounds in the elbow and in the area of the chest. He was hit by a hunting gun in the chest. And the other gunshot came from a different kind of firearm, a military firearm. I don't know what kind. The -- these objects were found in his body at the surgery ward of the hospital in Uzice. When getting out of that village when he was wounded, he managed to get into a creek, too, where he hid underneath a tree that had been felled and that was there on the creek. He lay there wounded for a longer period of time. I don't know how long. For several hours. People heard him crying and calling out for help, and they tried to save him. They tried to rescue him. One of the men who came there to try to help him also got killed while rescuing him. Another man went missing after that. For a long time we did not know what happened to him. He was found between the villages of Bradjevina and Magasici, dead. He had also been killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did your brother tell you who injured him, who shot him?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were looking for my brother in the wheat fields. They wanted to catch him alive. They did not find him in the place where they had wounded him. The pigs belonging to our other neighbours from the village were in that wheat field, too. They were moving about as well. These Muslim extremists that I mentioned a few minutes ago lost him because of those pigs. This Rade Jovanovic who tried to save my brother came across this group of extremists, and they killed him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: When you say they were looking for him, could you clarify for us who they -- you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Muslim extremists.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And when you say "Muslim extremists," are you speaking about soldiers or civilians?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It's one and the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Could you tell us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Richardson, he needs to answer the question whether to him these were soldiers or whether they were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I was going to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's an important distinction.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I was going to seek clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: When you say "soldiers," -- well, let me say this. You previously testified that civilians and soldiers were involved in the attack on your village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And so when you say "the extremists," are you referring to those soldiers and civilians who attacked your village?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: What are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Extremists are all persons in uniform who carried weapons, regardless of the type of uniform they wore.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Okay. Without labelling them as extremists, let's put aside that label for a moment, were they soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you. What happened to your brother with respect to the injuries he received that day in Bradjevina? He was treated. Did he ever heal from those injuries?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He never healed completely. He was given medical treatment at the surgery ward at the Uzice hospital. After having been ill for a long time due to these wounds, he died after a great deal of suffering in 1998 in Skelani.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that someone died who helped your brother. This was Rade Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Rade Jovanovic. He got killed at that moment. It's not that he was just dead.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Okay. How did he die, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Skelani, or rather in Bajina Basta with my brother. And I heard that Rade Jovanovic had been transported to Bajina Basta in order to have a post-mortem carried out. I went there to have a look. I saw the body. His head had been bashed badly. He had probably been beaten with all kinds of objects; who knows what. Either his left or his right leg had been completely severed due to the effect of some kind of weapon. So that's what I saw as far as Rade Jovanovic was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you -- when you went to Bajina Basta, you observed the body of Rade Jovanovic. Did you see any other bodies that you -- people who died during the attack on your village and the neighbouring villages?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the body of Stojan Stevanovic as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this: Was Stojan Stevanovic in the military as far as you know, the Serb military?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Was Rade Jovanovic a member of the Serb military?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Was Ljubisa Gajic part of the Serb military?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And from the village of Magudovici, one of the other villages that was attacked on the same day, do you know of anyone else who died during that attack?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slavko Petrovic got killed when he tried to get to Bradjevina. Novica Stjepanovic [as interpreted] got killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Were either of these men part of the Serb military?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. I see here Novica Stjepanovic. Is it Stjepanovic or Stanojevic? Novica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Novica Stanojevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just for the record. Because in line 4 of page -- not line 4. Line 5 we have Stjepanovic. It's not Stjepanovic; it's Stanojevic. Yes. But of course, repeat the same question because it's the other question that's relevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Were either Novica Stanojevic or Slavko Petrovic part of the Serb military?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And was your brother a member -- either of your brothers members of the Serb military?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And specifically so that it's clear, I'm referring to in June of 1992 or any part of 1992 that you're aware of. Could you answer verbally.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you. An individual by the name of Vukoman Pavlovic, are you familiar with him?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did he also die during the attack?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you know where he was from?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Grabovacka Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And are you aware of whether or not he was a member of the Serb military?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you know how he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No means you were not aware or no you know that he wasn't a member of the Serb army? Was he -- do you know whether he was a member of the Serb army or not or not? If you know, you should be in a position to tell us yes or no then.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was not a member of the Serb army or any other formation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: He died during the attack on Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you know what the circumstances are surrounding his death? Now, you mentioned he was from Grabovacka Rijeka. Did he happen to be in the village at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. With Rade Jovanovic he went up there to the village to see what he could do to help, whether he could get someone out, things like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And he was killed during this time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But no one knows under which circumstances. Rade got killed when he was looking for my brother, whereas this man got killed at some later point. He was simply found between these two villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like to take you back to when you arrived at Grabovacka Rijeka with your family and other members of the villages in the surrounding areas. Could you tell us what happened when you got to Grabovacka Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we came to Grabovacka Rijeka, the people were there crying, screaming. They took us in. We stayed there for a while in order to be able to get our wounded to the other bank of the Drina River. We spent the night there that night. When I managed to get my mother and father to the other side of the river on a small boat, during the night at 11.00 at night, my wounded brother Stevan came. We managed to get him to Serbia, too, on a small boat. I returned to Grabovacka Rijeka from the Drina. I spent the night there. In the morning, I set out towards Skelani on foot with my brother Slavko. So I got to Skelani and I don't know what happened after that at Grabovacka Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there any reason that you yourself didn't go into Serbia with your parents?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the right-hand river bank of the Drina River, that was in Serbia, there was civilian police and military police. And they didn't allow anyone, any individual, to cross the Drina into the other state. They allowed no able-bodied men to cross, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, if you could briefly tell us after you arrived in Skelani, did you join the territorial forces there -- Territorial Defence, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not right away, but several days later, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And could you just tell us, was -- when you joined, was this voluntary on your part or was it involuntary? Were you mobilised?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: No to which question? Were you mobilised?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't voluntary.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: So you were mobilised?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Well, did you receive anything from the Serb military or -- in the area of Skelani advising you that you had to serve the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived in Skelani from Grabovacka Rijeka, I crossed into Serbian territory to stay with my brother who had a house in Bajina Basta, and my parents were there too. My brother Stevan was still at the hospital in Uzice. I wanted to go and see him there. In Bajina Basta municipality, I was stopped by a military police patrol. I was ID'd but I had no documents on me at that point. Everything remained behind in my village and burned down. They took me back to Bosnia and Herzegovina territory, more specifically to Skelani. I reported to a recruitment office of some sort that was there, or rather the TO. I was given a uniform with TO Skelani insignia. I was given a rifle. I remained there until the 16th of January, 1993, until the attack on Skelani.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Could you tell us -- you said you remained there on January -- until January 16th of 1993. Where did you go after you left Skelani? Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Back to Bajina Basta in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And did there come a time that you returned to Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Well, when did you return? What year and month, if you remember.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime in late 1995, possibly early 1996. I can't remember the specific date.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did you serve the -- were you a member of the Serb military forces between the periods of June 1992 until after you returned to Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1995? Please don't answer that question. I'm going to restate it more clearly. Were you a member of the Serb military forces following January of 1993?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And specifically, this is with respect to the Serb military forces in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was never a member of any military unit after the 16th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Could I have a moment, Your Honour? Your Honour, thank you. At this time I would ask the usher's assistance. I would like the witness to be shown a particular document Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and we do have copies for Your Honours as well as for the Defence. What is being handed out at the moment is a B/C/S document. We do have an English translation -- an English translation of just the title of the document I should say. If the usher can show the witness -- and I'd like it to have it premarked for identification purposes only.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, could you take a look at that document, specifically the title. Could you -- this document is dated November 4th, 1994 -- November 11th, excuse me, 1994. The top left-hand corner of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam, 11/4 here means 11th April, not 4th of November.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you. As you can see, I often revert back to the US way of dating.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: So this document is -- maybe you can just tell us the date. Is it correct it's dated April 4th, 1994 [sic], and it makes reference to the 3rd Infantry Battalion. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: That's fine. But as you're reading it now, at the top left-hand corner it's dated April 4th, 1994 [sic]?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And it has to do with a 3rd -- conscripts receiving a packets of clothing, and it's a list. I would refer you to -- it's not numbered, page numbered, but if you could turn to what is ERN number 01316685.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: If the usher could assist, I would greatly appreciate it. It's midway through the document. The usher will assist you. That's 6685. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And if you would look midway what is titled -- well, I guess I should say your name is on this page, just not on number 17 of the list of names which is towards the end of the page. Just take a moment.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that. I found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And this refers to an infantry company. I would ask -- there is a signature across from your name, and I would ask if that is your signature and are you familiar -- well, first, is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you know who signed -- do you know this signature? Do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did you authorise anyone to receive clothing or sign on your behalf for any items from the Serb military?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No one ever asked anything like that of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And other than the clothing that you received when you were in Skelani in 1993 - the clothing, the rifle - did you receive any items from the Serb military in 1994?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And were you a member of this company that's listed under ERN 668 -- 6685 at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Next I would ask the usher's assistance once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you tendering this?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I am not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So this is not being tendered in evidence. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I do have another document I would like the witness to be shown and we would like the usher's assistance once again. This document should be marked for identification purposes only. This -- the next document I will show the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: If you just take a look at that document for a moment, it has to do with conscripts of Fakovici. Is that correct? If you look at the title. Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And your name appears on a list of individuals. My first question to you is: Are you familiar with these individuals on the list?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Stanisa Stevanovic. I know Slavko Stevanovic, my brother; and Milica Stevanovic, a relative. I know their names, but I have no idea how they came to be on this list.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Were you ever a member of the conscript from Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And this list purports to be delivery of flour, soap, and other hygienic products. Did you receive any products from the Serb military in 1993, hygienic products?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never got anything from the Serb army because at the time I was in Serbia, in Yugoslavia, and my mother was with the Red Cross in Bajina Basta.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, if you look at the date which is towards the end of this document, could you tell us if you were -- please tell us what date that is. Can you read it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 24th of December, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And where were you on this date?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was probably working somewhere around Obrenovac in Serbia as a construction worker. I can't remember specifically where, but I know that I left Bajina Basta to go to Obrenovac where my sister lived and I did work there as a construction worker.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Can you tell us if you know if any of the people you recognise on the list, were they conscripts from Fakovici, do you know, from the people that you recognise?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I heard, Stanisa Stevanovic was the only one who was a member of the TO following the attack against our village. He had a work obligation that had been assigned to him. He was doing some sowing or planting or whatever. He was the only person from my village who remained in Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I have another document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do you intend to do with this document, Ms. Richardson?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I apologise. I will not have this document tendered; it was marked for identification only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's marked for identification. We just need to mention the ERN number in the Serbian version, which is 01316667. It's not going to be marked further than that if it's not being tendered in evidence as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Next I would request the assistance of the usher again. Your Honour, I had handed out to the Defence as well as Your Honours what is a B/C/S version of a stack of documents as well as the English version. I would have the usher assist us with the -- have the usher assist the witness with reading the B/C/S version and locating the area that I would have a couple questions for him. The ERN number is 00685048.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: It is a list of names. The ERN number for the English version, this is for Your Honours and for the Defence is 000567 and that has been translated. Now, I do just have one remark about this document and the English version versus the B/C/S version. The date at the top of this list, which is I believe attendees of anti-tank combat course, there is a -- there appears to be on the B/C/S version a handwritten indication of the date. On the English translation, the date appears to be different -- well, I should have the witness read and then we can see what date that he -- what date this appears to be to him and then we can take it from there. Mr. Stevanovic, look at the list of the names, and to the top right-hand corner could you tell us -- well, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And is it -- in B/C/S it says it's a list of the attendees of an anti-tank combat course. Just at the top, the title of the document. Is that what it appears to be to you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And to the right of that there is a handwritten indication of the date. Could you tell us what that date is.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date is beginning with the 14th of August through to the 18th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you. If you look at this list, your name appears. Can you find it. It's under the 5th Infantry Battalion, just in the interests of time. Do you see your name?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see my own first and last name, but there must be other people who have the same name as I do. It could have been any of those other people who go by the same name.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. My question is: Were you a member of the 5th Infantry Battalion in 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And if you look at the other individuals who are listed under the 5th Infantry Battalion, are you familiar with any of those individuals?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know none of these people here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Okay. And do you recall where you were in 1995. Were you in Serbia or had you returned to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which period of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Of the date of this document which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: August of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: August of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was also working as a construction worker somewhere or other at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did you attend any training course with the Serb military in 1995 or prior to?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. I was a member of the JNA. I took an oath and I did my regular military service.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And what year was this, so we're clear?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: That's all the questions I have with respect to this particular document. Thank you to the usher for her assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you tendering this?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I apologise yet again. I'm not tendering this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Stevanovic, I have a final series of questions for you. Did you speak with -- do you recall a conversation in Skelani that you had regarding Bradjevina recently?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And could you tell us what -- who you had this conversation with and where were you and if you recall what day this occurred.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on a Wednesday. I think the 26th or 27th. That must have been the date. I was sitting in cafe called the Dragan's Water in Skelani. While I was there a young man came over with a woman. I didn't know these two. They sat down at a table and asked to speak to the owner. As they talked I realised that the woman had sold her house - she was a Muslim - to the landlord of that cafe. She came to collect her money, the money that he had not yet given to her. And he was accompanied by this driver, or rather the man who was with her. As they talked, someone asked the young man where he was from. He was sitting behind me at a different table. He said he was from a village called Mocevici. I turned around, faced him. I was glad to see him. I asked him who he was, what his name was. And he told me his name was Nezir Jakubovic and that he was Mujcin Jakubovic's son. Before that I had been in Srebrenica. I read the names on the donation lists at the entrance to the municipal building in the corridor, and one of the names was Nezir Jakubovic, but I had a different person in mind who I used to know and he was a good deal older than this person. And I asked this young man now whether he was the recipient of this donation. And he answered: No, I can't tell you exactly whether that man had been killed or whether he was sick, the one I asked him about. He said: My name is Nezir, my last name is Jakubovic, and that it was his name on that list. I congratulated him on that. Obviously I wanted the very same thing, to have my house back and to go back to my property. I asked him where he lived at the time. He said somewhere around Tuzla. I told him what my name was. We started talking. We started saying something about the village of Oparci. I asked him whether he knew anything about the three brothers who had gone missing during the war, and he said he only knew that they had been taken alive to Srebrenica. And nothing was heard of them later. We also talked about other aspects of the story in connection with Bradjevina and Magudovici. He told me that when they were about to attack those two villages his unit from Mocevici commanded by a man named Akif - and I don't know his last name. The Muslim unit from Mocevici was directed towards Kaludra. He told them that they were familiar with the road and that they should attack Kaludra. Once they finished attacking Kaludra, they should go back through Mocevici, or rather through my own village of Bradjevina. He told me that they found no one alive or dead in Kaludra. The people had gone days before the attack; they had left the village. They were astounded themselves to find no one there he said. They went straight back to my own village, Bradjevina. When they entered the village, he said they found Stojan right there in the middle of the village and that his throat had been cut. I asked him if he knew who did that and he wouldn't answer. On the way out they found my oxen out in the meadow. They picked them up and drove them to Mocevici. I asked him who the oxen were staying with and he wouldn't say, but he said that they were being used because they were strong animals. He said that the command centre of the Muslim army had taken them over and used them to drive ammunition from one place to another, used them as draft animals or to transport food and large weapons such as anti-aircraft guns that they couldn't carry, mortars as well -- as well as missiles, or rather shells. That is more or less everything about my encounter with this person. I also asked him whether Naser [Realtime transcript read in error "Nasir"] had been the one who attacked my village. He said he didn't know. Akif took over command from Naser, he said, and was in charge of that particular attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Let me just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Since yesterday or last week my attention was drawn to the fact that Nasir and Naser are not the same name, and I see that the transcript says Nasir. Did you say Nasir or Naser?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So for the transcript that should appear Naser and not Nasir. I'm sorry to interrupt you, Ms. Richardson, but it was important.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can ask him, because he said 26th and 27th, but he didn't say of which month and which year.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: That's correct. I was going there next.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Could you tell us. You said 26th. What month are you referring to, and which year, that you had this conversation with this person in Skelani.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was just recently before I came to testify, maybe two or three days earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: So are we talking October?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we can stop here for the time being. We go for our break. We will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Proceed, Ms. Richardson, and try to conclude, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In fact, I have just a few questions left.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, you mentioned -- before the break you were talking about a -- you were testifying about a conversation you had with Nezir Jakubovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Jakubovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Jakubovic in Skelani. Now, with respect to the information that he gave you, he told you about three brothers being kidnapped and also seeing the body of Stojan. Did he tell you about any other of the victims that died during the attack in Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He just told me that he saw these victims.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Which victims? Other than Stojan, which victims? Which other victims?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He saw Slavko.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And what did he tell you --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slavko Petrovic. He saw Novica Stanojevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did he tell you the details surrounding their deaths? Did he give you any information?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He just told me about Novica, that he would not have been killed had he not taken the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Which --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had he hidden somewhere, they wouldn't have found him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: "They" meaning who? So we're clear.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Novica Stanojevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And you said: "They would not have found him." Who was he referring to, Nezir. Nezir. Who was "they" he was referring to?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Himself and the unit that he was in.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: You mentioned as well that Akif had given Nezir orders or instructions about going to Kaludra. Could you tell us if he mentioned the names or made reference to anyone else as a commander or as part of the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't tell him directly. He referred to the entire unit that he was in. Akif issued the order to the unit from Mocevici, that they should all go and attack Kaludra.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And did he mention the name of anyone who was maybe the overall commander?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that Akif was the commander of this operation against the Serb villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And did he mention anyone else who was part of the Muslim forces with respect to the attack?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not mention any other commanders involved to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And with respect to Akif, did he say who Akif was and what -- where he was with respect -- who he was with respect to the Muslim forces, other than the fact that he was the commander. Do you recall what he said?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall. He said that Akif and Zulfo Tosun were the two closest associates of commander Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, I have one final question, Your Honour. And I would ask the usher's assistance again. It was one of the same documents I referred to earlier. It's the B/C/S version of reference to ERN 6677. It's again the document with a list of names.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: If you can just locate again your name --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: If the usher could assist us in locating number 6685.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: It's the same page that you referred to earlier. Thank you. And your name is number 17. Above your name, I neglected to ask you earlier, there's another Stevanovic mentioned -- there are two others, actually. Slavko. Are you familiar with Slavko?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's my brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. And was he serving -- was he a member of the Serb forces in 1994, do you know?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 28th of June when we came to Skelani and when we crossed the Drina River, from that moment onwards he never returned to the territory of the present-day Republika Srpska or at that time the former Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: So this would -- and across from his name is a signature. Is that his signature? If you're familiar with his signature, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not his signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much to the usher. Your Honour, this completes my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Richardson. Mr. Jones. Mr. Jones is now going to cross-examine you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, I'm going to start by asking you some questions in relation to a map which you've been shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So if the witness could be shown P407, please. On the ELMO, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, if you could please take the pointer which you used earlier --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We seem to have some -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If you could take the pointer and if you could just move the pointer between Bradjevina and Ratkovici so we can just see the area between those two villages.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Bradjevina to Ratkovici in a straight line, actually. If you could trace a line between Bradjevina and Ratkovici.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Now, that distance as the crow flies between Bradjevina and Ratkovici is about three or four kilometres, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And now could you indicate the route which you would take if you were to walk from Bradjevina to Ratkovici, if you could just trace that on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he needs a pen or something with which he can highlight or track the route from Bradjevina to Ratkovici. Give him a black one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you put your initials at some point along that route, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Now, between Bradjevina and Ratkovici there are in fact hills and woods, aren't there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is nothing. We are on the other side of the river. When we go from Bradjevina to Ratkovici, there is a part from where I cannot see the lower area of Ratkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Well, let's move in if we can a bit more on the map, if we can zoom in on Bradjevina while keeping Ratkovici in the picture. I don't know if that's possible. Because I would like to focus in on a number which you see below Bradjevina which is 436 and it's the -- it's marking an elevation. There. I think we can see it now. Now, isn't it right that that marker 436 is an elevation or a hill of 436 metres just south of Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the very approaches to Ratkovici there are slopes, big rocks, from which I cannot see Ratkovici. And about 200 metres away from Ratkovici towards Bradjevina, there are meadows and you can see everything. From Bradjevina, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. And I'm asking you about these elevations which appear to be marked on the map. I'm asking whether you can confirm that those are hills. So we've looked at one there which says 436. There's another one further down, 374; and then another one to the left, 322. And then further down again 590.2. Now, isn't it right that those are all hills which are between Bradjevina and Ratkovici and that one of those is, well, 500 metres or so high? If you know, Mr. Stevanovic. It's a matter within your knowledge whether or not there are hills between Bradjevina and Ratkovici.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, I did not quite understand your question. I told you between Ratkovici and Bradjevina, in that area, there are thickets, woods, hills, but I don't think that they are that high up.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, let me put it this way --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Jones, because I saw Ms. Richardson stand up.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was just going to ask for counsel to clarify the question, but I think the witness himself indicated it was unclear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: My point is this: If you're standing in Bradjevina looking over towards Ratkovici, three or four kilometres away, with these features in between, you can't see, can you, what a person is wearing in Ratkovici from Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the village of Ratkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, could you also now indicate with a marker how you would get from Ratkovici to Mocevici, the route you would take.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Bradjevina to Mocevici?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: From Ratkovici to Mocevici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need the map to -- okay. Let him mark first and then we zoom later. He is going -- yeah. Now, the map needs to go higher. Yeah, that's it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, finally, could you mark on the map a place where yesterday you said there were fields which you shared - the villagers in Bradjevina - shared with the people in Magudovici. Could you mark where those -- that common area is.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So could this last line that you just plotted on the map, could you give it the letter V, V for Victor, and then put your initials next to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness should also mark the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I'm going to that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And the previous marking that you made from Ratkovici to Mocevici, could you put your initials next to the line, preferably between Dvoriste and Mocevici, your initials.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Mr. Stevanovic. Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you referred to the meadows where the people from Ratkovici kept their sheds, as I think they were called, where they keep their cattle, and you said that was towards Poznanovici and partly towards Mocevici. Now, could you mark on the map where those meadows of the people from Ratkovici are located.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: People from Ratkovici, Donji Ratkovici. This is a village that cannot be seen from my village. Towards Poznanovici, up there, there is Potocari and Gornji Ratkovici, two more villages, that is. I said yesterday that I saw cattle being herded out of Kaludra, Ratkovici, and Bradjevina, not further up. Not towards Mocevici. That is actually the way they took the cattle out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes -- yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I can refer to the transcript, at least the draft transcript which we have from yesterday. It was lines 131059 to 131109. And the witness said: "But where the sheds were in the meadows where people kept their cattle, these -- where I saw this towards Poznanovici and partly towards Mocevici."

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So I understand you to be saying that those meadows were towards Mocevici and Poznanovici. If that's not correct, then please feel free to correct me and mark on the map where those meadows are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Try to locate on the map and then mark Poznanovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Poznanovici is, I think, further down if we move the map down a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Put it -- put the name of the village in a circle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And put your initials next to it, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the meadows will be where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you put an "M," the letter "M," capital "M," against that line, please, and also put your initials.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, the witness has put the capital "M" immediately followed by an "S" which is only one of the -- of his initials. Yes, go ahead, Mr. Jones. Let's not complicate it further.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, I'm just going to ask you: Is that right? Did the people from Ratkovici really keep their cattle and livestock one or two kilometres from their village on the other side of a hill? Is that actually correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So they would leave their livestock several kilometres or a couple of kilometres anyway from the village where anyone could at night break in and help themselves?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. These are meadows and pastures where the cattle were and where these sheds were made.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And at night, then, the cattle would be kept near Ratkovici, right, not in the meadows?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depended on the cattle, and it depended on where people could make these sheds, whether they could make sheds in their own backyard or whether they had sheds in the meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And it's right, isn't it, that those meadows are, what, a kilometre away from Bradjevina? How far roughly in your estimation.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a crow flies, from my village to there, I don't think that there is more than 350 to 400 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, I think we can all see it on the map what -- the line you've drawn is roughly halfway, or perhaps a little more than halfway, towards Ratkovici. Surely that would make it more like one kilometre or one and a half metres, given that it's three or four kilometres as the cry flies between Bradjevina and Ratkovici.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area of the meadows and all the villages - Madjevina [phoen], Bradjevina, Kaludra, Polimci, et cetera - these were enormous meadows, pastures where cattle were grazed and that is where all the people from these villages had their sheds. It's not on the road to Ratkovici, what I drew on the map, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would hate to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Just for the purpose of establishing the record. The term "as the crow flies," if we could -- I'm not sure if this will be clear later on in the transcript. Some people may understand what that means, some others may not. The witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The important thing is that the witness understands and that we understand, and I think we all understand what the term means.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Well, I believe this map is to scale anyway, so we can presumably measure the distance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I hope, as I said earlier on, that we will be able to go on-site and be able to visualise the terrain and distances for ourselves. But we certainly can rest assured, madam, that we are fully aware of what the term means.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, moving on to another subject. You mentioned yesterday a number of incidents which you attributed to the break down of relations between Serbs and Muslims, and you referred to the killing of Goran Zekic as one of them.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you some questions about Goran Zekic and his killing. Goran Zekic was the president of the SDS in Srebrenica, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And he led the Serb takeover of Srebrenica on the 18th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, are you aware that Goran Zekic went into Srebrenica from Bratunac with armed men, including Arkan's Tigers from Serbia, and took the town over?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, Goran Zekic worked and lived in Srebrenica. He owned a flat there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, do you know of Arkan's Tigers, the gang of Zeljko Raznjatovic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I read about them in the press.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you've spoken today about Muslim extremists, and if I understand correctly for you anyone in a uniform who was a Muslim was an extremist. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who were under the command of Akif and Mr. Oric.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
